extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, scientists, and learned men seeking a method for inquiry
extracted.subtask_description: Methodological guidance for conducting natural philosophy: how to move from sensory experience to sound axioms and useful inventions through regulated experiment, avoiding authority, superstition, and fruitless procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path from the senses to the understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: The way that leads from the senses to the understanding must be properly prepared; the present methods do not well prepare that passage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissensions and the variety of schools show that current methods fail to connect sensory observation to sound intellectual principles; a correct method should reliably translate sense-data into understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unanimity is not confirmation of truth
rubrics_metrics.description: True unanimity proceeds from a free judgment arriving at the same conclusion after investigation; mere concurrence or authority-driven assent is not proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware of regarding wide assent as evidence of truth — unanimity often reflects prejudice, authority, or obsequious concurrence rather than free reasoned agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distrust reverence for antiquity and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Reverence for antiquity and the authority of famous authors retards advancement; truth is the daughter of time, not of authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allow respect for ancient writers or established authorities to block investigation; prefer observation and accumulated time-tested evidence over deference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim science at useful effects and inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The legitimate goal of the sciences is the endowment of human life with new inventions and riches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific inquiry should pursue practical new effects and useful inventions rather than merely producing material for lectures, fame, or contemplative satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate natural philosophy with particular sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural philosophy must be applied to particular sciences, and particular sciences must be referred back to natural philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without this integration (rooting specialized fields in natural philosophy) disciplines like astronomy, optics, music, medicine, and political science lack depth and glide over surface phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid beginning discovery by surveying authorities and inward reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: A common (faulty) method of discovery is to first obtain all that has been said by others and then add private reflection — a method without foundation that turns on opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not start inquiry by cataloging past writings and invoking internal inspiration; this approach yields opinion, not discovery. Begin from experience structured by method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logic (as commonly used) does not discover first axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: Discoveries of logic are not discoveries of principles and leading axioms, but only of what appears to accord with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on scholastic logic to find first principles; logical methods may test conformity but do not replace experiment-driven discovery of fundamentals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a regulated, digested order of experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The real order of experience begins by setting up a light, commencing with a regulated and digested, not a misplaced and vague course of experiment, and thence deducing axioms, and from those axioms new experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize experiments systematically (not chance or groping). Establish a clear protocol: controlled observations -> derived axioms -> designed experiments to test and expand those axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value particulars and experiments; do not disdain them
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a prejudicial conceit that the dignity of the mind is lowered by intercourse with experiments and particulars; experiments are essential though mean and laborious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid contempt for experimental labor and detailed investigation; frequent, patient work with particulars is necessary to reach solid principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not mistake refined craft for deep knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Admiration of the effects and artifices of mechanical arts can make men inclined to admire wealth rather than perceive poverty in scientific understanding; many crafts depend upon few axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not confuse mechanical skill, refinement, or elaborate apparatus with genuine increase in scientific knowledge — seek the underlying axioms rather than surface complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid passing off superficial improvements as real discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Polishing old discoveries, making them more elegant or combining them, often passes off as new discovery, though it is not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize claims of novelty: distinguish between cosmetic refinements or recombinations and truly new principles or effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reject genuine novelty because of impostors
rubrics_metrics.description: The absurdity of impostors promises and fantastical claims has fostered prejudice against new propositions, but this should not cause rejection of all new attempts especially when coupled with mention of effects to be produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious of extravagant claims, but do not let previous charlatans extinguish inquiry; evaluate new proposals on evidence and method, not merely on the company they keep.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against superstition and improper mixing of religion and philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Superstition and immoderate zeal for religion have opposed natural philosophy; mixing divinity and philosophical authority often excludes novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep theological authority from unduly suppressing natural inquiry; natural philosophy, rightly pursued, supports faith and is not antithetical to religion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions must not chain inquiry to canonical writings
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities and schools often order lectures so that anything out of the common track can scarcely enter minds; men are chained down to the writings of particular authors and dissenters are attacked as turbulent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational institutions should permit liberty of thought and encourage deviation from standard authorities to foster progress; avoid curricular and social structures that punish innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare minds with hope and practical reasons for inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Men’s despair and the idea of impossibility repress attempts; we must prepare men’s minds and disclose reasons for not thinking hope improbable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate reasonable hope by presenting concrete reasons and preliminary indications (examples like Columbus) that legitimate the pursuit of new discoveries; psychological readiness is part of scientific progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ organized instruments of discovery (Tables of Invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use arranged and digested tools (Tables of Invention) to bring particulars into order and to serve as the basis for experiments and axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with systematic collections and tables that guide investigation — these are the objects of hope and practical instruments for discovery (referenced as part of the Instauration).
